title: Tensions flare in Hyderabad after eggs 'thrown' at idol during procession
description: Hindu organisations protested following an incident where eggs were allegedly thrown at a Durga Mata idol. The incident occurred during an immersion procession within Madanapet police station limits in Hyderabad. Police responded promptly after receiving a call and took the suspects into custody for investigation. A similar incident involving stone-pelting was reported during a Durga Visarjan procession in Maharashtra.

title: ‘VIP culture’ in hospitals can compromise patient safety, equitable care: AIIMS doctors
description: Pressure from influential patients can lead to unnecessary medical procedures and a longer recovery time for others. Surgical oncologists at AIIMS Delhi emphasize that this practice undermines equal treatment for all patients. Prolonged hospital stays for VIPs can also negatively impact hospital resources and staff morale. The authors advocate for appropriate clinical protocols and transparent admission criteria to ensure fair patient care.

title: Protests engulf Europe: People take to streets in France, Albania, Italy, Spain, Portugal
description: Thousands of people protested across Europe over the weekend, demanding action against rising living costs and government corruption. Demonstrations were reported in France, Italy, Albania, Spain, and Portugal, with varying degrees of violence. Clashes between protesters and police resulted in numerous arrests and injuries in several countries. Many demonstrators called for affordable housing, better education, and protection of public pensions.

title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan shift donations towards AI and science
description: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan are investing $50 million to establish STEM labs and an AI center at Sacramento State University. This generous donation aims to transform vacant state office buildings into a thriving downtown campus. California Governor Gavin Newsom emphasized this initiative will enhance the tech job talent pipeline, while the couple shifts their philanthropic efforts toward biomedical AI, aligning with Meta’s vision for innovation and education.

title: Couple die waiting for accident compensation in son’s death case
New York court orders review of jailed mother's $500 child support cap claim

Chelsea Four-Rosenbaum had sought to limit her debt to $500, arguing that her income remained below federal poverty guidelines while imprisoned. An appeals court ruled that her request had been examined under the wrong legal provision and ordered a fresh review.

title: In first-ever climate crisis amends, Nepal to get $21.6 million
description: The decision taken this week by the UN body, the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD), in its emergency meeting assumes significance as it is not only a kind of admission that climate change causes such extreme events, but also an endorsement of the principle that historical polluters (developed nations) must contribute to the fund to assist vulnerable developing countries.

title: ‘200 seats haq hai hamara’: Congress puts its UP poll ambitions on Lucknow walls
description: Posters demanding 200 Assembly seats have surfaced outside the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee headquarters in Lucknow. Congress aims to strengthen its position ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections by negotiating a larger seat share. The party has reportedly submitted a wishlist to its ally, Samajwadi Party, complicating seat-sharing discussions. State Congress leaders are using a grading model to evaluate constituencies based on organisational growth.

title: Were they beheaded? Bangladesh seeks answers from Saudi over execution of 'couple'
description: Bangladesh has requested detailed information from Saudi Arabia about the execution of two citizens. The two individuals were executed for committing an indecent act inside a mosque in Makkah. A diplomatic letter was sent seeking clarification on their legal representation during trials and other circumstances. Dhaka is also looking for explanations regarding discrepancies in the charges against these citizens.

title: Kentucky court orders fresh review of $703,000 farm dispute after divorce
description: Mary and Fred Holden's property settlement agreed to equal ownership of their Kentucky farm. Disagreements arose regarding when the farm should be listed for sale after two years. After their son moved out, Mary requested the farm be sold or purchased by Fred. The appeals court found the agreement's wording ambiguous, requiring a fresh evaluation in family court.

title: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis expand $10M beach house after mudslides
description: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis are planning a significant renovation of their Carpinteria beachfront property. The proposed changes include expanding the main residence and adding a swimming pool. They acquired the property in 2017 for $10.1 million and have seen its estimated value rise to about $17 million. The couple's plans involve the removal of a guest cottage to enhance the outdoor living space.

title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says US rules pushed China toward self-reliance
description: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang pointed out that US export controls have significantly fueled China's semiconductor advancements. He remarked that these restrictions have compelled China to bolster its own chip production strengths. Huang also expressed strong faith in the US technology sector's resilience, despite heightened competition from China, and dismissed worries about an impending memory chip surplus, predicting ongoing demand for High Bandwidth Memory in the years ahead.

title: IIT Madras graduates' hostel idea grows into over 1,500 foldable buildings
description: Modulus Housing, founded by IIT Madras graduates, focuses on manufacturing foldable buildings for quick assembly and transportation. Since 2018, it has provided over 1,500 modular structures across India and parts of Africa. The startup aims to improve access to essential infrastructure like schools and clinics, especially in rural areas. Recently, it raised ₹70 crore in funding to support further expansion and innovation.

Following recent comments from US President Donald Trump, fears of renewed military action against Iran are escalating. Araghchi emphasized the need for rationality to avoid another military confrontation.

Elevated oil prices and inflation concerns are contributing to deteriorating corporate earnings outlooks affecting investor confidence. Domestic institutional investors have somewhat mitigated the selling pressure on markets in recent weeks.

title: 'When will you score runs?' Babar Azam's weaknesses exposed by ex-Pakistan player

He scored 45 against Sri Lanka and 34 against England, failing to build on important beginnings. Former cricketer Tanveer Ahmed has highlighted weaknesses in Babar's batting against spinners, incoming fast deliveries, and short balls. He emphasized the need for Babar to address these vulnerabilities to improve his performance.

title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches

He emphasized that doing so would strengthen the 'Vocal for Local' campaign and promote a self-reliant India. Modi highlighted successful local exports such as makhana and arhar dal to various international markets. Additionally, he discussed efforts aimed at reviving traditional skills and farming practices, including natural cotton cultivation.

title: From unfinished books to 10-second reels: Is reading becoming lost art?
description: The growing preference for short-form digital content is raising concerns about children’s ability to engage with books and sustain attention. Educationists and experts examine declining reading habits, the role of examination-driven learning, and the impact of digital distractions. Drawing on research and Kerala’s library movement, the story explores ways to rebuild deep reading through schools, families and communities.

title: Drone attack: Iran targets Kurdish opposition bases in Iraq
description: Iran's armed forces conducted a drone attack on the Komala group in Iraq's Kurdistan region. This operation reportedly caused significant damage and casualties to the group's infrastructure. Previous strikes on the Komala group have occurred since the regional conflict began in February. Iran accuses these opposition groups of receiving support from Israel, its longstanding adversary. The Kurdish opposition has denied allegations of receiving arms from Israel despite Iran's claims.

title: Five IPOs to hit Dalal Street next week, targeting nearly Rs 2,600 cr from investors

title: Centre rushes 250 RAF personnel to Arunachal after protests over hydropower project

A mob torched an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, injuring over 40 police personnel. The project, seen as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam, faces opposition from indigenous tribes fearing displacement and submergence of villages.

title: Man spits gutkha from 3rd-floor balcony, dies after coming in contact with 11kV wire

Residents reported that his spit, while chewing gutkha, made contact with the 11kV line. Locals expressed anger towards the electricity company for neglecting their complaints about unsafe wiring. His landlord mentioned that officials had assured residents about addressing these high-tension line concerns.

title: ‘Failed to pay rent’: How landlord’s complaint led to 1,600 fake Rs 500 notes

title: 'Don't be spectator, show leadership': EAM Jaishankar to UN on terrorism, global crises

He highlighted a significant gap in global decision-making that leaves many regions, particularly in the Global South, behind in critical areas like finance, fuel, food, and fertilizer. Emphasizing the importance of fair AI development, Jaishankar encourages strategies that ensure widespread access to its benefits, fostering international cooperation.

Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, lake views and potential damage to an aging sewer line, with one neighbor citing $75,000 in repair costs. Kelce’s construction team says it has spent $7,500 on sewer repairs and adjusted the plans. However, local officials require further changes before the remaining landscaping work can proceed.
